_comment: Noise allowance per row for assert-perf-gate.py, on top of the 1.00
ceiling. The gate compares medians-of-medians over `runs` shots of three
arms measured in ONE job on ONE runner, so what is left to absorb is
same-machine shot-to-shot noise, not the CPU-model lottery perf-budgets.json
has to live with. A row is a breach when candidate/reference exceeds
1 + margin; the geomean over all rows gets `geomean` and nothing else.
Seeded from same-runner repeats (chromium perf-probe.yml runs=5, EPYC and
Xeon draws): the median-of-medians CV was 0.00-0.01 on int_math, js_alloc,
libm_fmod, locator_click, layout, screenshot and 0.02-0.05 on the
page-driving rows (goto_cold the widest). `tight` covers the first group,
`default` the second, `loose` the rows perf-budgets.json documents as
dispersion-bound even after repeats (webkit eval_rtt / click_force).
Every gate run prints the observed CV per row in its summary; tune a
margin from those, not from a failed run's ratio -- and read the CV
beside the `tick` column, never alone. A CV cannot tell a precise row
from a quantized one: WebKit clamps performance.now() to 1 ms, so its
in-page rows repeat the same integer on every shot and read the LOWEST
CVs on the board. That is how libm_fmod, seeded here off chromium's
5 us clock, landed on a `tight` margin its own clock could never
resolve. The gate now flags any margin thinner than two ticks.
firefox WAS in `loose` (launch, js_alloc) and came back out once the gate
had printed enough CV columns to size the two rows. The entry was copied
from perf-budgets.json's dispersion-bound list, which is about the
cross-run CPU-model lottery — something this gate structurally does not
have, since all three arms share one job on one runner. Measured here
instead: firefox launch reads cv 0.018 / 0.028 / 0.042 across three gate
runs, so a 1.10 ceiling was 2.4-5.6x its own noise and a real 7% launch
regression would have promoted. js_alloc never took the loose margin at
all — `tight` is tested first and lists it — and at cv 0.009-0.012 it
should not: 1.03 is already about 2.5x its noise, and the 1.065 that
row read on 799bdf7 was a real regression, not spread.
webkit's two rows came out 2026-09-25 and `loose` now holds no browser
at all. It kept them on the strength of perf-budgets.json's `TIGHT ROWS`
note -- "every webkit row except eval_rtt/click_force" -- which is a
statement about n=1 shots across four CPU models. This gate is n=5 with
three arms in one job on one runner and structurally has no CPU lottery,
the same provenance defect that retired firefox's entry. Four runs now
exist (every other job on record reads `skipped` -- it runs only when
webkit is actually rebuilt), all on EPYC 9V74, and they measure
eval_rtt cv 0.004-0.024 and click_force cv 0.002-0.054: a 1.10 ceiling
was 4x and 2x their own noise. Both now take `default` 0.06, which every
one of the four runs still clears.
What the two rows actually are decided it. eval_rtt is the node<->CDP
round trip -- same node, same Playwright, same protocol on all three
arms -- so it is a NULL CONTROL that should read 1.00, and a control
free to swing 9% detects nothing. It is a candidate for `tight` once a
second CPU prices it; its worst draw is 1.028, too thin to move today.
click_force is the opposite: three quarters of it is browser work (hit
testing, event dispatch, layout) that codegen really does reach, and it
reads 1.023-1.043 against official in ALL FOUR draws while its ratchet
sits at parity. That is a standing gap, not spread -- musl's scalar
memset/memcpy against glibc AVX2, the same shape the chromium input
profile isolated -- and 1.10 was calling it green. At 0.06 it reads as
the tie it is, with 0.017 of headroom; if that gap widens the gate will
red a build that did not regress, and that is the intended behaviour.
DISCONTINUITY 2026-09-25: runtime-probe.cjs took libm_fmod from 9M to
36M iterations to put it above the 1 ms tick. The row's absolute
milliseconds are ~4x what every earlier run recorded, on ALL browsers.
Ratios stay comparable, raw times do not.

loose._note: No browser takes this margin today; add a browser key to grant it.
